title: Research Lab Distribution Survival / Exit Timing
question: Can framework distribution/pullback evidence materially improve staged exit timing versus price-only or hold baselines without excessive premature exits?
hypothesis: A small subset of point-in-time framework signals may add useful pre-crash lead time, but only if they survive false-exit, re-entry, multiplicity and price-only baseline tests.
baseline: HOLD plus simple price-only drawdown/trend baselines, with tier-aware volatility and no exact-top objective.
required_analysis: Separate historical-as-was from current-machine retro replay.
Reject any result that depends on revised data before historical knowledge time.
Quantify drawdown avoided and upside surrendered jointly.
Include false alarms, recovered warnings and missed drawdowns.
Compare staged trim policies only as research counterfactuals.
Penalize correlated signals and multiple testing.
Prefer simple combinations and leave-one-signal-out tests.
Recommend prospective confirmation only after historical falsification survives.
falsifier: Warnings add no useful lead beyond price, or false exits/whipsaw consume the avoided drawdown benefit.
kill_condition: If no signal family adds robust incremental decision value across admissible episodes and controls, retain distribution monitoring as context only and do not create an exit engine.
